notes.claim: A shorted lead acid battery can deliver 100 to 1000 times the typical discharge current used in most applications.
Short circuit current is typically estimated by dividing the open circuit voltage by the internal resistance.
The peak short-circuit current a battery can deliver is limited by its internal resistance, including the intercell connectors.
One test on a 480 V battery predicted 2550 A from 480 V over 0.160 plus 0.028 ohm, close to a measured average of 2530 A.
Short circuit current stays relatively high at low states of charge: it exceeded 90 per cent of nominal even at about 60 per cent charge.
Exposed metal parts of the battery always carry a voltage and are electrically live, with a risk of short circuits.
A battery short reaches its steady maximum current within 5 to 10 milliseconds in one measured test. (added for i8)
Batteries contain little inductance, so a shorted battery behaves much like a fault through a resistor. (added for i8)
Accurate short-circuit current and resistance values are needed to size and select the circuit protection device. (added for i8)
Total DC short-circuit current is the sum of what the battery, the charger and motors deliver. (added for i8)
One maker's 12 V 70 Ah block lists a short-circuit current of 1814 A and an internal resistance of 6.95 milliohms (a data row). (added for i8)
Electrolyte is highly corrosive; wash any splash in eyes or on skin with plenty of clean water and seek immediate medical help. (added for i8)
Switch off all electrical circuits before connecting or disconnecting batteries. (added for i8)
Do not rest metal objects such as tools on top of a battery. (added for i8)
Battery electrolytes usually contain either sulphuric acid or potassium hydroxide. (added for i8)
These very corrosive electrolytes can permanently damage the eyes and cause serious chemical burns to the skin. (added for i8)
A nickel-cadmium cell's low voltage of 1.20 V means many cells are needed for a high voltage. (added for i8)
The standard nickel-cadmium cell is one of the most rugged and forgiving batteries. (added for i8)
Nickel-cadmium's potassium hydroxide electrolyte is not used in the chemical reaction, so measuring it does not track the charge. (added for i8)
A lithium-ion cell's nominal voltage is 3.60 V. (added for i8)
Lithium-ion needs a protection circuit to prevent thermal runaway if stressed. (added for i8)
Lithium-ion is safe provided its voltage and current limits are respected. (added for i8)
BS 7671 Amendment 4 (2026) adds a new chapter covering stationary secondary batteries. (added for i8)
A metal tool shorting a battery's terminals gets very hot very quickly, and if it explodes its molten metal can burn and ignite explosive gases. (added for i8)
A lithium-ion cell's electrolyte is a lithium salt in an organic solvent, and it is highly flammable. (added for i8)
